rules.statement: Each solution MUST identify its business capability and accountable owner.
Applications MUST communicate through documented contracts and identify data owners.
Technology selections SHOULD follow a supported lifecycle and require justification for new platforms.
Every production solution MUST document context, deployables, repositories, owners, and external dependencies.
Trust boundaries, data flows, failure modes, and deployment topology MUST be documented.
Solutions MUST pin their standards baseline and record scoped exceptions.
Frontend and backend MUST have separate application repositories and release pipelines.
Features MUST NOT import another feature’s internal implementation; use its documented public API or app-level composition.
HTTP calls MUST pass through the approved API client layer; generated files MUST NOT be manually edited.
Business-specific logic MUST stay in its feature and shared code MUST NOT depend on features.
UI MUST provide accessible keyboard navigation, semantic controls, and loading, empty, and failure states.
Domain MUST NOT depend on Application, Infrastructure, API, HTTP, or persistence frameworks.
Application MUST NOT depend on Infrastructure or API.
Infrastructure MUST implement ports owned by Application or Domain.
Endpoints MUST delegate business decisions to application/domain code and enforce documented authorization.
Module data MUST be accessed through its owned interfaces; cross-module writes MUST NOT bypass ownership.
rules.verification: Module dependency tests and data review

rules.statement: Every persistent store and schema MUST have a named owning application/module and data steward.
Schema changes MUST use committed migrations with expand/contract compatibility across supported releases.
rules.verification: Migration rehearsal and mixed-version integration tests

rules.statement: Relational integrity MUST use constraints where applicable; indexes MUST be justified by measured access patterns.
rules.verification: Constraint tests and query plan review

rules.statement: Runtime database identities MUST have least privilege and MUST NOT perform production schema administration.
Production stores MUST define RPO/RTO, retention, backup encryption, and restore-test evidence.
HTTP APIs MUST publish versioned OpenAPI artifacts and use a documented error contract.
Breaking contract changes MUST retain a documented migration and supported compatibility window.
rules.verification: Contract diff and consumer compatibility tests

rules.statement: Mutation retries MUST account for idempotency and ambiguous network outcomes.
Trace context MUST propagate across supported boundaries without secrets or sensitive payloads in telemetry.
Application pipelines MUST independently build, test, and release immutable artifacts.
Changes MUST run applicable unit, architecture, integration, contract, security, and critical journey checks.
Production workloads MUST emit structured logs, useful metrics, traces, and readiness/liveness signals without exposing sensitive data.
Secrets MUST be supplied through approved secret management and MUST NOT appear in source, images, or logs.
Infrastructure MUST be version-controlled with reviewed plans and controlled production apply identities.
Data stores MUST use restricted network access and documented ingress/egress paths.
Production topology MUST document failure domains, capacity assumptions, DNS, certificates, and recovery dependencies.
Every exposed operation MUST define authentication and server-enforced authorization, including resource ownership.
Solutions MUST document threats, trust boundaries, data classification, and mitigation owners.
Browser applications MUST NOT contain confidential credentials and token/session handling MUST follow the documented identity design.
Sensitive data MUST have defined encryption, retention, deletion, and telemetry redaction controls.
